subject: Re: Platform fee amortization, support tiers, and license structure for Clearwater private deployment
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@clearwaterhealth.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Guerrero <t.guerrero@clearwaterhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment pricing questions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency profile and the KV cache behavior. Before we can move to procurement, our finance and infra teams need clarity on a couple of points in your private deployment pricing:

1) Platform fee amortization: can the platform fee be treated as a capitalized cost over the initial contract term (3 years), or do you treat it fully as an annual operating charge? We need language for our CAPEX/ OPEX teams.

2) Licensing unit: are licenses sold per-GPU, per-host, or per-concurrent-request? We have a mixed cluster (on-prem + private cloud) and need predictable scaling costs.

3) Support tiers: we need 24x7 incident support and an on-call SLA for production incidents. What do your premium support and enterprise support tiers include (response times, included hours, escalation matrix)?

4) Discounts & multi-year: what's possible with a 36-month commitment and a two-region deployment?

If you can send a short worksheet and a sample clause for our procurement team, that would be great. Happy to jump on a call with Tom (cc'd) tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
VP, Digital Platforms
Clearwater Health

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@clearwaterhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing questions

Hi Samantha — great to hear the demo was useful. Quick answers up front, and I attached a worksheet (Redwood_Private_Pricing_v3.xlsx) with line-item examples.

- Platform fee: by default we invoice the platform fee annually as an operating charge. We can provide contract language to allow CAPEX-style amortization (customer accounting decision) and offer an invoice schedule to match. For procurement wording, see sheet tab "PlatformFee_Wording".
- Licensing units: primary commercial model is per-reserved-capacity (GPU-pool) plus a small per-concurrent-request runtime surcharge for burst traffic. For on-prem, customers can opt for host-bound licensing (per-server) if that fits their CMDB.
- Support tiers: Premium includes 24x7 Slack + phone, 2-hour P1 response, 1-business-day P2; Enterprise adds a named technical account manager, quarterly on-site reviews, and 24/7 escalation to engineering.
- Discounts: for 36-month commitments with two-region deployment we typically offer a 22–28% uplift on list depending on committed GPU capacity and payment terms.

Tom/Procurement — if you can confirm target GPU equivalent and preferred billing cadence (annual vs upfront), we can run final pricing.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Guerrero <t.guerrero@clearwaterhealth.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@clearwaterhealth.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 08:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing questions

Thanks Priyom — a few clarifications from our side:

- Target: we expect to reserve the equivalent of 8 A100-class GPUs initially, with burst to an additional 4 GPUs in the second year.
- Billing cadence: preferred is annual with option to prepay for year 1 to secure discount.
- CAPEX language: procurement would like contract language that explicitly states the platform fee can be invoiced as a one-time upfront 'platform capitalization' invoice that would allow them to treat it as CAPEX. Is that something Redwood can accommodate, and would that affect discounting?

Also, on support: we need guaranteed on-call rotation with a named engineer and an SLA that includes updated runbooks after any Sev1.

Can you share a redlineable clause for the platform fee capitalization and an example support-SLA?

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Infrastructure Projects

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:25:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment pricing questions

Priyom — forwarding Tom's note. For this deal (8 reserved GPUs -> 12 year 2), I'm proposing we:

- Offer a one-time platform capitalization invoice for year 1 equivalent to 12 months of the platform fee, payable upfront. That lets procurement capitalize.
- Apply a 26% net discount on list for a 36-month commitment with year-1 prepay.
- Include Enterprise support (named TAM + 24x7 escalation) as part of the package for the first year, then bill the support as a % of platform fee in years 2–3 unless they renew.

Questions for Marcus: need approval for the 26% discount band and the support inclusion for year 1 at our cost. Also propose a $75k migration credit if they sign by end of Q1 to offset internal integration work.

Laura

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment pricing questions

Laura — saw the ask. Approve the structure with the following constraints:

- Discount: 26% is acceptable provided the deal is commit-to-spend (36-month) and we have a non-cancellable, non-refundable upfront payment for year 1.
- Platform capitalization invoice: ok to provide a one-time upfront invoice that procurement can treat as CAPEX; legal to include language that it is invoiced as a prepayment for platform services over the contracted term.
- Enterprise support included year 1: approved, but include a clause for transition to a paid support % in year 2 (we need clarity on baseline included hours).
- Migration credit: approve up to $50k rather than $75k; any incremental credits require head of revenue sign-off.

Also ensure commercial clause that allows us to reclaim unused reserved capacity if usage falls below 60% for two consecutive quarters.

Marcus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@clearwaterhealth.com>, Tom Guerrero <t.guerrero@clearwaterhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Platform fee capitalization + final commercial terms (RDW-4789-CW)

Hi Samantha & Tom — thanks for the patience. Attaching the redlineable clause and an updated worksheet (Redwood_Private_Pricing_v3.xlsx - v3) that reflects Marcus-approved terms. Highlights: 

- 36-month term, 8 reserved-GPU equivalent (year 1) -> bump to 12 in year 2.
- One-time platform capitalization invoice: we will invoice 12 months of platform fee upfront, labeled in the SOW as "Platform Capitalization Prepayment". Legal has added language that it constitutes prepayment for platform services over the contract term (suitable for CAPEX treatment by customer accounting).
- Commercial: 26% net discount for year 1 with year-1 prepay; subsequent years invoiced annually at the same discounted rate unless renegotiated.
- Support: Enterprise support included at no additional cost for year 1 (named TAM, 2-hour P1 SLA, runbook updates after each Sev1). Year 2+ support will be charged at 12% of platform fee unless opted into a higher support package.
- Migration credit: $50,000 credit applied on first invoice for integration work if signed before 2026-03-31.
- Capacity protection: clause to reclaim unused reserved capacity if utilization < 60% for two consecutive quarters; we will include a one-time rebaseline discussion before any reclaim action.

Next steps:
1) I'll send the DocuSign bundle with the SOW + pricing schedule and the platform capitalization clause.
2) If you want, we can schedule a 30-min legal-to-legal call to walk procurement through the wording.

Links: DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-clearwater (preview). HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/678901/RDW-4789

If that looks good I'll route for signature.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
Attachments referenced: Redwood_Private_Pricing_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), Clearwater_MA_plan.pdf (procurement notes)
